Subject: Intermittent control-plane timeouts after sidecar rollout (Brightline Labs)

Hi Jonas —

We started observing intermittent control-plane timeouts across our private deployment this morning after we applied the sidecar upgrade you pushed yesterday (v1.1.2). Symptoms: agent reconnects, short-lived failures of management RPCs, and two customer-facing model latency spikes (customers saw 503-style errors for ~30–90s).

Timeline we saw:
- 07:42 PDT: healthchecks start showing increased latency
- 08:05 PDT: several agents reconnect (kube events show LIVENESS probes firing)
- 08:07–08:12 PDT: customer-facing errors reported

We collected a couple of excerpts from the agent logs — attaching sanitized snippets. We can jump on a bridge if useful; impact is production but limited to a subset of nodes (not all regions).

Can you confirm whether this rollout included the sidecar config propagation changes? We rolled back the application pods on our side but the control-plane errors persisted for ~15 minutes after.

Thanks for the quick help — Elaine

Quick technical update from the runtime team after the bridge and initial log review.

Summary / root cause hypothesis (preliminary):
- The v1.1.2 sidecar introduced an async config propagation path that delays heartbeat bootstrap on first connect when there is concurrent pod restart churn.
- On nodes with high agent churn we saw heartbeats stall for ~10–45s while the sidecar waited for config blobs; the management plane treated these as timeouts and triggered upstream reconnects.
- This aligns with the agent reconnect window you reported and the timing of the 503 spikes.

Immediate mitigations applied during the bridge:
- We pushed a temporary configuration to increase heartbeat timeout window from 5s -> 60s (reduces reconnects while we validate).
- We rolled back the async propagation patch on the control plane for the Brightline cluster only (patch id: RB-priv-2026-05-24-a).

Next steps (action items):
1) We will publish a one-off patch (privnet-sidecar-patch-1.1.2.diff) that changes startup ordering and adds a short, bounded retry loop for config fetch. We recommend applying to all affected nodes. (Attached.)
2) Update the runbook with a pre-check that detects high churn and automatically enlarges heartbeat windows during upgrades (privnet-runbook-kb.md).
3) We'll schedule a non-urgent follow-up to fully test the async propagation path and CI gating.

Evidence attached: minimal repro logs and the diff file. We will follow up with a full post-incident writeup and timeline within 48 hours.

Notes to Brightline: we will credit a portion of May's invoice for the window of reduced SLA — we'll confirm numbers after the postmortem.

Regards,

Elaine — thanks again for working with us over the weekend. Below is a concise summary and planned follow-ups. Full postmortem (timeline, logs, fix plan, and credit calculation) is at: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcD-example-postmortem (Brightline internal viewable link).

Incident summary (short):
- Impact window: 2026-05-23 07:42 PDT -> 2026-05-23 09:05 PDT (primary observed service disruption).
- Root cause (prelim): race condition introduced in sidecar v1.1.2 async config propagation causing heartbeat stalls under concurrent pod churn.
- Scope: subset of nodes in Brightline Labs' private cluster; not a full-region outage.

Resolution applied:
- Emergency increase of heartbeat timeout to 60s to prevent reconnection cascades.
- Rollback of async propagation change for Brightline cluster.
- One-off patch attached for immediate application; full fix to be code-reviewed and released after QA.

Planned follow-up:
- Engineering postmortem call: Thu, 2026-05-28 09:00 PDT (invites to follow).
- Permanent fix timeline: target staging release 2026-06-03, production roll on 2026-06-10 pending regression tests.
- Billing credit: we will apply a pro-rated credit for the impacted minutes; finance will follow up with numbers by Wed 2026-05-27.

Attachments included in this thread: bridge-invite.ics, diag-collect.sh, privnet-sidecar-patch-1.1.2.diff, privnet-runbook-kb.md
